messages:
carla-support: heads-up: Cascade reported intermittent 429s during a 10-min marketing burst this morning. They’re on a Dedicated pool. Happened ~09:12-09:22 UTC. 

brian_sre: thanks — can you paste baseline/peak QPS and pool config?

carla-support: baseline ~35 qps stable; burst peaked at ~420 qps for ~3 mins. Their dedicated pool is 4xA10g, autoscale enabled, target_util=0.7, max_nodes=6. They've got a per-request concurrency of 8.

alice-ng: any 429 response headers? retry-after?

dan-customer-eng: from the logs we see 429s with Retry-After: 10 and response body: {"error":"rate_limit","message":"quota exhausted"}. Repro curl attached: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer XXX" -d '{"input":"x"}' 

carla-support: repro steps from customer: scripted fanout of 500 concurrent short requests over 3m -> ~420 qps. They expect some throttling but observed client-facing 429s even though pool wasn't at max_nodes constantly.

brian_sre: graph snippet: 09:10-09:25 queue_length spikes to 1800, 95p latency jumps from 120ms -> 2.3s, node_util hits ~88% on 4 nodes then scale starts but cooldown delays based on policy.

infra-bot: autoscale event: scale_up triggered at 09:14, step=1, cooldown=120s. New node ready 09:17.

alice-ng: sounds like scale_up step and cooldown are too conservative for sudden short bursts. If policy only adds 1 node and cooldown is 120s, a 3-min burst won't be covered quickly.

brian_sre: agree. Two things to validate: 1) noisy neighbor (other customers on same pool?) 2) per-route throttles/limits logic on the load balancer. Any batch jobs at same time?

dan-customer-eng: customer confirms no heavy batch jobs on their side. They were running many small requests from many clients. They expect the Dedicated pool to handle this traffic pattern.

carla-support: checked tenancy: pool is shared across a single account (their dedicated) — not multi-tenant. No noisy neighbor inside pool, but internal queuing due to concurrency limits per model instance is apparent.

alice-ng: suggested quick mitigation: temporarily increase max_nodes to 8 and scale_up_step to 2, reduce cooldown to 30s. Also add a soft per-route qps limit (e.g., 300 qps) to smooth spikes.

brian_sre: operational risk: increasing max_nodes will increase cost. Recommend temporary bump for the marketing window + retro config change. Also propose adding headroom target 60% (instead of 70%) for similar customers with bursty patterns.

carla-support: I pushed a change proposal to the customer tenant: max_nodes=8, autoscale: {"scale_up_step":2,"cooldown":30}, target_util=0.6. Waiting approval.

deploy-bot: deploy started for tenant cascade: update-autoscale-config v2 -> in_progress at 2026-03-17T09:35:12Z

infra-bot: deploy complete: update-autoscale-config v2 at 2026-03-17T09:37:05Z

dan-customer-eng: after the change we ran the same synthetic burst, peak ~430 qps, 95p latency now 240ms, no 429s. Looks good. Thanks.

brian_sre: follow-ups: (1) add an evaluation rule to suggest lower target_util for bursty workloads, (2) add optional faster ramp policy (burst-mode) users can opt into, (3) instrument per-tenant queue length alert when backlog >1000.

carla-support: ACTIONS: @brian_sre to file infra ticket for burst-mode autoscaler config; @alice-ng to add eval rule and doc blurb; @dan-customer-eng confirm if they want permanent max_nodes=8 or revert after campaign.

dan-customer-eng: they'll keep 8 for 48h then reassess. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

carla-support: closing the escal for now, will reopen if any regressions. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
